items.title: A Repair Estimate Is Not Necessarily a Notice of Bad Faith in Louisiana
items.summary: A Louisiana insurer received a contractor's estimate far above what it paid after a hurricane, and the insured sued for bad faith penalties 60 days later. Federal courts in Louisiana have held that an estimate describing damage is not by itself notice of a statutory violation, and they have stayed suits until proper notice is given. The Louisiana Supreme Court is still considering the issue. Louisiana law, so persuasive context only for Missouri work.

items.title: California Adds Voluntary Review Before Insurers File Rate Applications
items.summary: California is adding an optional review step before insurers formally file rate changes. The Department of Insurance can publish its early rate estimates and concerns first. It applies to property and casualty insurers, who can opt in or go straight to the standard filing.

items.title: Why BofA still sees an October Fed rate hike
items.summary: BofA analysts still see a strong case for a Fed rate hike in October, pointing to September inflation and a core PCE reading that could reach about 3.4 percent by year end. The market prices only about a 20 percent chance of a hike at the October 28 meeting.

items.title: This Week In Running: October 19, 2026
items.summary: Francesco Puppi won the Grand Trail des Templiers in 6:32, one second off Jon Albon's 2021 course record, and Martyna Mlynarczyk won the women's race in 7:41. Hugo Deck won the longest ever Diagonale des Fous in 22:54, and Ruth Croft won the women's race in 27:13, her third win among the sport's four best known 100 mile races.
